title: The everyday Odisha table
lead: Start with a small bowl. Follow a fruit, a handful of badi, a leaf-wrapped parcel—and the people who make them memorable.
intro: These stories begin with named cooks, family memories and photographs of real food. Read one before your visit, keep a dish in your journey, and leave room for the version your host knows.

chapters.title: A little sour, a little sweet
chapters.text: Follow elephant apple into a relish, then into one family’s memory of Kartik.

chapters.title: The pleasure of a small accompaniment
chapters.text: Dried dumplings, coarsely crushed: a way into pakhala, preservation and the maker’s story.

chapters.title: A fruit, a season, a slice
chapters.text: Meet a ripe-palm-fruit preparation, with a golden centre and questions to take to the cook.

questions: Who taught you to make this?
What changes with the season or occasion?
contribution: Know another preparation or remember someone who made it? Share the dish’s local name, place and your connection to the story. Ask permission before sharing another person’s words or photographs.
limits: Named accounts and photographs, not a restaurant directory or a universal Odia menu. Local names, spellings and preparations remain open to community review.
